question: how do i find out why my financial aid hasnt shown up yet and who do i talk to

body.answer:

For all other aid shown as a Memo, the page strongly recommends contacting the Office of Financial Aid to resolve outstanding issues. [2]

Contact the Office of Financial Aid: email finaid@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7549. It is in E-210 (Academic Building). You can request an in-person appointment by email or through the chat on its website; appointments are Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm. The office says most questions can also be handled by phone, Webex, or email. [5][7]

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
For Spring 2027, Student Accounts offers a four- or five-month Ramapo Tuition Payment Plan (RTPP), beginning November 16, 2026. Enroll online by logging into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/) before the semester’s posted payment deadline. Pay the down payment and setup fee when you enroll. The five-month plan requires 20% down; the four-month plan requires 25%. [1]

Spring installments are scheduled December–April for the five-month plan, or January–April for the four-month plan. Additional payments are due on the 15th of each month after enrollment. [1, 3, 5] The plan has no interest. There is a non-refundable $60 setup fee, also described as a $60 service fee. [1, 2]

Past-due balances from previous semesters of $500 or more must be paid before you’re eligible; the College may deny enrollment based on past payment history. Enrolling after the down-payment due date requires paying missed installments at enrollment. Missing the payment deadline may result in a $200 late fee and/or deregistration. [1]

Questions: Student Accounts, (201) 684-7495 or studentaccts@ramapo.edu. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts handles credit-balance refunds. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check, mailed to your billing/permanent address; it will not go to a campus mailbox and cannot be picked up at Student Accounts. Direct deposit is optional and free. [1]

To sign up: [3]
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/
2. Locate the Student Account Info card; click Bill & Payment Suite, then Electronic Refunds on the right under My Profile Setup.
3. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if previously completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify.
4. Click Payment Profile; edit an existing saved Payment Method or create a new one. Check the box in Refund Option to designate it as the direct-deposit refund account.

An eligible refund is expected within one to two weeks of submitting the application. [2] Title IV aid overpayments resulting in a credit balance of $1.00 or greater are refunded; non-Title IV financial aid has a $5.00 threshold. [1] The fastest way to receive a refund is direct deposit. [7]

Questions: Student Accounts, studentaccts@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7495; D-Wing, First Floor. [1, 2]

question: whats the deadline to file the FAFSA for next year and what does ramapo need from me besides that

body.answer:
For 2027–2028, the FAFSA is open [8]. If you’re a new student, sections 1 and 8 say to submit by May 1; section 7 instead says no later than March 15. The pages differ. If you’re a returning student, section 8 says apply by April 1. Section 6 recommends applying before March 1, but does not call that a deadline. You need to file once each academic year [5, 11].

Ramapo’s Financial Aid office says complete the FAFSA at studentaid.gov using school code 009344; no other forms are required [9]. If you’re applying through the EOF Program, you must file the FAFSA or NJAFA by March 1. Documents needed to complete or update the application include federal tax returns for you and your parents, untaxed-income documents (such as Social Security or public assistance award letters), investment records, and bank statements [2].

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
A student may NOT withdraw from a course after the published deadline [3]. Deadlines are posted on the Academic Calendar: https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/ [3]. The pages describe a possible late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances: ordinarily, apply before the end of the semester; explain why standard withdrawal procedures could not be followed, state the term, and provide appropriate documentation. It typically results in W grades for all courses in that term; ordinarily, only one term per appeal [5]. The provided page text does not give the application form or submission instructions. The Registrar says an approved course withdrawal after the refund period records a W and gives no refund [3]; that is not permission to withdraw after the deadline.

Withdrawing may affect financial aid and satisfactory progress toward graduation [1]. For a withdrawal after the refund period, federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when aid is fully disbursed [10]. SAP eligibility is reviewed annually after spring; students who do not meet its standards lose financial aid eligibility [7]. These pages do not establish whether your particular course withdrawal will affect your aid or SAP status. Contact Financial Aid to discuss your circumstances: finaid@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7549, E-210 [10].

Contact the Registrar about the deadline or withdrawal process: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224 [3].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/)

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts: Add your parent as an Authorized User to let them make payments on your behalf. [1]

1. Log into RCNJ Experience: https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/ [4]
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click “Bill & Payment Suite.” [4]
3. Click “Authorized Users” on the right side of the page in the My Profile Setup section, then click the “Add Authorized User” tab. [4]
4. Enter your parent’s email address, answer questions, and click “Continue.” Click the “I Agree” box, then “Continue.” [4]

If you want them to pay but not see your bill or payment history, select “No” for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history.” [3] An authorized user receives an email link, username and password to access the Bill and Payment Suite. [3]

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
Public Safety handles permits. Applications are online only [9]. Section 10 directs you to the RCNJ Parking Permits portal: select permit type; complete contact information and click “Save/Update Person,” then “Continue”; enter vehicle information; review and continue; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number. It is application verification, not your permit. Select “student” and the correct commuter status. Permits for new students are available at New Student Check-In [10]. Questions: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu; include your Ramapo student ID # (R#) [3]. Public Safety: (201) 684-7432 [10].

It says to print a temporary permit from “MY,” display it on the dashboard until the permanent permit arrives by mail, then activate the mailed permit online [11].
The permit fee and New Jersey sales tax are added to the term bill; the 6.63% tax applies to off-campus students [9].
Commuters receive a hangtag for the rearview mirror; park in your appropriate lot [4]. All students may use C1, C2, or D lots as overflow if their assigned lot is full [5]. Limited additional overflow parking is behind the tennis courts of Halifax Road [7]. Commuters may not leave a vehicle overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization [5].

question: how do i set up my campus email and wifi login

body.answer:
**Email — Registrar:** New students: visit [Ramapo e-mail](https://password.ramapo.edu/) and click “Activate E-mail Account.” You’re eligible to set it up within 24 hours of receiving your Ramapo ID number; a valid Ramapo email account is required to register for classes. If you forget your username or password, contact Ramapo ITS. [2]

**Wi-Fi — ResNET:** On your device, scan for wireless networks and connect; see the [Wireless page](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/secure-wireless/). [11]
• iPad: Open Settings > Wi-Fi, select Ramapo-Secure, enter your Ramapo username and password, then click Accept at the certificate warning. [5]
• Android: Open Settings > Wi-Fi and select Ramapo-Secure. Set EAP Method: PEAP; Phase 2 Authentication: None; CA Certificate: Use system certificates; Domain: ramapo.edu; Identity: YourRamapoUsername; Password: YourAccountPassword. Tap Connect. [8]
• Windows 8: Select Ramapo-Secure in the available wireless networks, enter your Ramapo username and password, then click Connect at the warning. [7]
For device registration, determine whether you’ll use wired or wireless, retrieve the MAC address for that connection, and use the [wired](https://resnet.ramapo.edu/register/login.php) or [wireless](http://mydevices.ramapo.edu/) registration link. Instructions for finding your MAC address are [here](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/getmac/). [9][10]

For email help, IT Help Desk: helpdesk@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7777. [2] For Wi-Fi help, ResNET: resnet@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-6831. [5]

question: do transfer students need to take all the gen ed / Intellectual Inquiry requirements again or do some get waived?

body.answer:
No—not necessarily. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all General Education requirements under the transfer-credit and waiver policies. [3]

If you transfer with at least 48 credits but without a completed A.A. or A.S., you are waived from some requirements. The listed waived keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities. You must still complete Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and one course from each of two distribution categories at Ramapo: Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society. Advisement will identify applicable waivers and remaining requirements. [1][2]

If you complete an A.A. or A.S. at a New Jersey community college, General Education requirements are waived after Ramapo receives your final official transcript showing the conferred degree. A.A.S. graduates do not get a full waiver; courses are evaluated individually. [8]

Generally, only transfer credits accepted in your semester of matriculation are considered for possible General Education waivers. [4] The pages describe General Education waivers, but don’t specifically explain whether “Intellectual Inquiry” is a separate requirement. [1][3]

For your individual waivers, contact the Office of the Provost at provost@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7330. [1] For transfer-credit questions, contact Admissions at admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300. [8]

question: I got a parking ticket yesterday because my permit was still processing. how do I appeal it and who do I email

body.answer:

The listed reasons not considered include ignorance of regulations and disagreement with the rules; the pages do not say whether a permit still processing is an accepted appeal ground [1][2][10].

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
The Office of Student Conduct handles the conduct process. The pages describe a meeting with a Hearing Officer/College Disciplinary Review Board as an opportunity to discuss what happened, but do not say whether you personally must attend a hearing. Contact the office to ask what applies to your case: studentconduct@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7869, C-212. [1][3]

If the candle led to a fire-alarm activation, the published sanctions for a first violation are a $150 fine and a fire-safety reflection: section 2 says “completion of a Fire Safety Reflection Sanction”; section 4 says “completion of a fire safety reflection assignment.” The pages differ in wording. [2][4] The pages do not establish that an alarm was activated or state the outcome of your write-up. [2][4]

If you are preparing for a hearing, you may submit signed, dated, typed or clearly written statements or documents to Student Conduct before it; first-hand witnesses may submit statements and may be called. You may request to review the statements and incident reports used in the case by contacting the office to arrange an appointment or request the file; you may not duplicate the materials. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/recommended-judicial-sanctions/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/frequently-asked-questions/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/)

question: how do i apply to graduate? i'm a senior finishing in december

body.answer:
The Registrar says all candidates must apply. [3]

1. Make an appointment with your advisor to confirm you are ready to apply. Your advisor will remove your graduation hold, giving you access to the online application. Your degree audit “MUST have all areas satisfied.” If it needs an adjustment, email your advisor or convener before applying; they will contact your dean with recommended adjustments. [2]
2. Complete the online Graduation Application after your advisor meeting and approval. [2,8] The page also gives these steps: log on to the [Experience Webapp](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/); locate Student Self-Service Card; click Open Student Dashboard; select Student Profile; select the Spring term with the down arrow (top left above the photo spot); click on Application to Graduate (Link on left side of page); fill in the information and submit. [4]

question: how do I get credit for my internship? I need to register for it but dont know where to start

body.answer:
Start with the Cahill Career Development Center. Its career advisor starts the intake process and checks eligibility; the Center assists with registration procedures. [1,4]

After you’re accepted for a co-op internship:
1. Select and meet with a co-op faculty advisor to determine learning objectives and academic assignment. [1]
2. Request a co-op Experience on Handshake: http://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/. [1,2]
3. Meet with your career advisor and receive “Registration Permission” from the Career Center. [1]
4. Complete the appropriate form with Academic Advisement if you select Pass/Fail. International students on a J1 or other visa must get authorization from the international advisor and fill out the appropriate paperwork. [1]
5. Register through “Self Service” on “My Ramapo” to add the co-op course. Registration authorization only gives permission to take the course. [1]

The experience must be a learning experience applying classroom knowledge, with transferable skills, defined dates and job description, learning objectives related to your academic/career goals, professional supervision and routine feedback, and employer resources supporting learning. [3] The co-op Experience Request has student, employer, and faculty-advisor parts; a Learning Agreement must be approved by your faculty advisor, career advisor, and employment supervisor. [6,8] Students must attend orientation and reflection sessions. [8]

Credit: the Career Center page lists 2 credits for at least 120 hours and 4 credits for at least 240 hours within the semester, based on start date; co-op is available fall, spring, and summer only. [2] The catalog says each successfully completed co-op course is 4 credits. The pages differ on credit options. [8] Up to 8 credits may count toward graduation; additional co-op credits do not count toward graduation. [4,8]

Contact Cahill Career Development Center: careercenter@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7444 (Main Office, C-209) or (201) 684-7675 (ASB Office, ASB-513). [1]

question: What do I need to do to move out of my dorm when I graduate? is there a checkout process and what happens if I'm late

body.answer:
Housing & Residence Life’s published end-of-spring checkout guidance says to follow the checklist before leaving. Remove trash and recyclables; leave the College refrigerator on at level 5; remove personal items; set the thermostat to auto, low, at 70°F; clean your room; close blinds, lock windows, turn off lights, close the door, empty your campus mailbox, update correspondents with your new mailing address, and leave drawers open. Leave by your checkout deadline, based on your last exam schedule. [1] All students must review and follow the checklist: https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/ [2]

If you need to stay past the designated checkout date and time, complete the Check-Out Extension Request process: https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/. Extensions are not granted for non-academic reasons, including unavailable/late transportation and off-campus employment. Approved extensions do not allow guests. [6]

Not vacating as required or failing to abide by posted checkout times may result in a $75 improper-checkout fine. Excessive garbage is $25 per bag; damage charges are determined case by case. [2][4] Final inspections occur after halls and apartments are vacated; failed inspections or prohibited items may be billed, and items left behind are discarded. [9] Damage, missing College property, or policy violations may also result in a post-checkout billing notice by email. [7]

These pages don’t give a graduation-specific checkout date or separate graduate process. Ask your RA or Hall office before checkout. For help, contact Housing & Residence Life at reslife@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7461. [1]
